newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville Thurs power offers mostly up $1/MWh.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville Thurs power offers mostly up $1/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) mostly raised its surplus power offers by $1.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Thursday, the agency said Wednesday.
BPA said it was offering up to 200 megawatts of firm power during peak demand hours at $13.00 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $14.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
The offer was a $1.00 per MWh rise over heavy load offers for Wednesday delivery.
Thursday firm off-peak prices were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.

BPA offered up to 200 MW of next-day non-firm power during morning and evening peaks (hours ending 0800-1000 and 1800-2000 PST) at $17.00 for Northwest and $18.00 for COB, an increase of $1.00 per MWh from offers for Wednesday.

Non-firm power prices for off-peak (0100-0600 and 2300-2400 PST) were unchanged at $9.00 for all deliveries, while prices for shoulder hours (0600-0700, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200) were separated at $10.00 for Northwest and $11.00 for COB, another $1.00 increase from offers for Wednesday.
BPA also offered displacement power during off-peak hours on Thursday unchanged at $7.00 per MWh.
